{{Quote|Remove all heads, you must, to bring down a Troig.|[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="RoF">''[[Reversal of Fortune]]''</ref>}}
The '''Troigs''' were a two-headed, multi-[[Limb/Legends|limbed]], [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Pollillus/Legends|Pollillus]]. The majority of Troigs had two heads and four arms, with one head controlling one set of arms independently of the other; nevertheless, most Troigs had only one primary hand and three off hands. Each head exhibited its own personality and volition. For a two-headed Troig, the ''Saprin'', or right head, was thought to be the source of qualities such as loyalty, faith, and cunning, while the ''Saprah'', or left head, was the source of features such as love, anger, and passion. Troigs with more than two heads were rare but celebrated in Troig culture. Heads remained constantly aware of one another, a circumstance that afforded members of the species great awareness of their surroundings. 

Each head had its own name; the full being took their name by joining the heads' names with the infix ''sin''. For instance, the [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]] announcer [[Fodesinbeed Annodue/Legends|Fodesinbeed Annodue]] was a Troig with individual heads named Fode and Beed. The name Fodesinbeed was used when referring to them to as a single individual.

The species was discovered by the [[Galactic community|wider galaxy]] shortly before the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] of [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. The Troigs proved eager to explore the [[Star/Legends|stars]], and several emigrated from their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. They exhibited great capacity to learn [[Language/Legends|languages]], and [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] remarked that if only one of a Troig's heads learned a language, the whole being could comprehend it. One of the first to explore [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] was a Troig known as [[Fodesinbeed Annodue/Legends|Fodesinbeed Annodue]], who eventually became famous as the preeminent [[Podracing/Legends|Podracing]] commentator in the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Another Troig, [[AndroosinLiann]], hosted the [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]]-based talk show ''[[Essence]]''. In the latter [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the Troig [[Dwuirsintabb]] made headlines when the head Dwuir requested surgical separation from his partner head, Tabb. Medical technology remained incapable of accommodating the request without [[Death/Legends|killing]] one of the heads even into the regime of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Is that one guy or two?|[[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]|<ref name="YCAC" />}}
[[File:FodesinbeedAnnodue-SWE.png|thumb|left|The heads of a single Troig often manifested very different facial features and colorations.]]
The Troigs were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] bipeds characterized by their multiple heads.<ref name="TRO 1" /> Each Troig had at least two heads, although very rare specimens were born with three or more. Despite the fact that each of the heads was for all practical purposes a unique individual with [[Gender/Legends|his or her]] own personality, memories, will, and skills,<ref name="NEGAS" /> the species' nervous system connected the heads together and gave them a limited [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] connection to one another. The nervous system thus allowed each head to send instantaneous warnings to the organism as a whole and help it avoid hazards, for instance.<ref name="TRO 1" /> The connection between Troig heads was so strong that if only one head learned a [[Language/Legends|language]], another head that shared the same body could understand the first head when he or she spoke the foreign tongue.<ref name="SOT 38">''[[Secrets of Tatooine]]''</ref> [[Sleep/Legends|Unconsciousness]] in one head did not necessitate a similar condition in the whole entity, although one effective technique for anyone in combat with a two-headed Troig was to bang the heads together to lead to dual loss of consciousness.<ref name="CN2 10">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> The [[Death/Legends|death]] of one head inevitably led to the demise of the entire specimen<ref name="NEGAS" /> unless advanced medical technology was available. With medical intervention, a bicephalous Troig's heads could theoretically be separated from one another, although only one head could survive such an operation.<ref name="HNN 50" />

The typical Troig [[Bone/Legends|cranium]] was roughly conical. The skull sloped backward from the brow before rounding off to a dome; it then tapered to a point at the top of the head. The cranium dropped down in the back, bulged out at the back of the head, and then sloped down toward the neck.<ref name="EIIG" /> Some Troig heads had short horns.<ref name="CSWE I 283-284">{{CSWECite|I|283&ndash;284|Fode and Beed}}</ref> Not all Troigs had [[Hair/Legends|hair]], but it grew on some Troig faces<ref name="HNN 50" /> and atop some Troig heads. The [[Color/Legends|color]] varied from brown<ref name="TRO 1" /> to green<ref name="SWR 15">[[Star Wars (1998) 15|''Star Wars'' (1998) 15]]</ref> or pink. The hair's consistency and thickness varied such that some Troigs had hair long enough to pull back into a topknot,<ref name="HNN 50" /> while others left it as short bristles.<ref name="PRT" />

Although each of a Troig's heads could exhibit radically different features, their faces were generally narrow with a roughly [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] structure of two [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], a [[Nose/Legends|nose]], and a [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]]. The eyes were wide-set<ref name="SWCTP" /> and featured slit pupils. The sclera could be either yellow<ref name="EIIG" /> or white,<ref name="TRO 1" /> while the iris came in shades of brown,<ref name="POTJ" /> yellow, orange,<ref name="SWCTP" /> red, and green.<ref name="PRT" /> Having multiple sets of eyes gave Troigs excellent peripheral vision and allowed them to monitor more than one object simultaneously.<ref name="POTJ" /> Heavy brows protected their visual organs, and fleshy growths sometimes grew from below the eyes and projected toward the sides of the head.<ref name="TRO 1" /> Each of a Troig's mouths was framed in a pair of mutable lips and housed a set of white [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] and a dark-pink tongue.<ref name="PRT" /> Some heads also featured a pair of thick growths along the bottoms of the cheeks that flanked the mouth. Troig noses showed great variation; some were short and flat, others tall and narrow.<ref name="TRO 1" /> Two small tentacles grew from each side of each head.<ref name="YCAC">''[[Star Wars: Yoda's Challenge Activity Center]]''</ref> Troigs also had [[Ear/Legends|ears]] with which to hear.<ref name="TRO 1" />

[[File:Troig_circus_performer.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Troigs had a single pair of legs and a long, spiked tail.]]
The necks that supported each head were long and agile and split from a common source at the top of the torso. There they met a sunken chest that supported the four shoulders,<ref name="POTJ" /> each attached to an [[Limb/Legends|arm]]. The two pairs of arms were situated one before the other such that the Troig had a frontmost and rearmost set, the forward pair situated slightly closer to the ground than the back pair.<ref name="SWCTP" /> The arms were attached to three-<ref name="TPM2">[[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace 2|''Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace'' 2]]</ref> or four-fingered hands<ref name="POTJ" /> with gray claws.<ref name="PRT" /> For two-headed Troigs, each head controlled one set of arms. Still, the Troig had only one hand capable of the same level of dexterity as a right- or left-handed being's preferred hand, so that the other three hands were less adept.<ref name="NEGAS" /> For instance, a Troig might wield four weapons simultaneously, but only one hand could do so with full agility. The synchronization of their hands was not developed enough in most cases to afford them extra climbing or grappling ability.<ref name="JC">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050623jc68|series=Jedi Counseling|text=68}}</ref> Nevertheless, Troigs learned to use their two heads in tandem to allow them to manipulate objects with multiple hands simultaneously,<ref name="CSWE III 264-265" /> and some were truly multi-dexterous.<ref name="SOT 38" />

The chest met a plump abdomen whose flesh came to a protruding crest at the median that extended from the sternum and down to the groin.<ref name="TRO 1" /> A wide posterior and hips<ref name="SWCTP" /> led to two relatively short,<ref name="CSWE III 264-265" /> thickset, digitigrade lower limbs with knobby ankles at their midpoints and conical, three-toed hooves at their extremities.<ref name="WOSW 162">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> The average member of the species stood between 1.96<ref name="TRO 1" /> and 2.00 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall.<ref name="NEGAS" /> A long, [[Whip (weapon)|whiplike]] tail with a spiked, knobby bulge at its end grew from the posterior.<ref name="TRO 1" />

Troigs sported several possible skin colorations. Cream, brown, black,<ref name="TRO 1" /> green, orange,<ref name="POTJ" /> pink,<ref name="HNN 50" /> red,<ref name="TRO 1" /> and yellow were all known.<ref name="TPM2" /> Often each of a Troig's heads displayed a different color scheme; one green head and one red head was the most common pattern for two-headed Troigs.<ref name="CSWE III 264-265" /> Even on the body, a single individual could have skin that varied in hue from one body part to another, like a dominant skin tone with a paler shade on the underbelly and the insides of the arms and legs.<ref name="TRO 1" /> Alternatively, a Troig might have one primary color mottled with another.<ref name="TPM2" /> Wrinkles covered the hide, often forming complex patterns. For instance, the skin of the necks and arms was striated with bands of deep-set creases.<ref name="SWCTP" />

==Society and culture==
Troigs were thought to be unique in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for having separate personalities that shared the same body.<ref name="TRO 1" /> Still, the degree of the heads' individuality was a matter of debate in medical and philosophical circles. On the one hand, the heads acted together to create a single sense of identity for a single Troig. A Troig's heads had a symbiotic relationship of mutual interdependence; they looked out for one another such that it was extremely difficult to surprise a Troig.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Indeed, certain personality traits were common among Troig heads, such as outgoing conviviality and curiosity.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|fodeandbeed|Fode and Beed}}</ref> On the other hand, the heads exhibited personalities that were unique from one another,<ref name="TRO 1" /> and each thought independently<ref name="CSWE III 264-265" /> to the point that a Troig might even have an argument with itself.<ref name="POTJ" /> The complexities of their multiple heads and personae gave problems to grammarians as well, since discussing Troigs brought up issues of whether to refer to a single entity with multiple personalities with singular or plural pronouns, and whether to refer to the entity as one Troig or as multiple Troigs. In general, however, common [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] practice was to count as one entity and use singular forms of words for the complete biological entity rather than the individual heads or personalities.<ref name="DB" />

For a two-headed Troig, the left head was referred to as ''Saprah''. The head was considered to be the source of "[[Blood/Legends|blood]] humors" that regulated powerful emotions such as anger, love, and passion. The right head, meanwhile, was called ''Saprin''. It was thought to be the source of "breath humors," which controlled the Troig's senses of cunning, faith, and loyalty. The rare Troigs born with more than two heads were highly revered in their society<ref name="NEGAS" /> to the point of becoming celebrities.<ref name="TRO 1" />

[[File:Trog_pilot.png|thumb|left|A Troig's heads manifested not only diverse physical features but diverse personalities as well.]]
Rarely, one head could develop mental illness and become detrimental to the organism as a whole. For that reason, Troig society recognized the necessity to medically separate heads in such circumstances. Nevertheless, well into the period of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]]-standard surgical techniques were not advanced enough to allow for separation without killing one of the heads.<ref name="NEGAS" />

On their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Pollillus/Legends|Pollillus]], Troigs held standard occupations, such as that of a [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomat]].<ref name="NEGTD 27">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> They had access only to relatively primitive technology.<ref name="CSWE III 35">{{CSWECite|III|35|Pollillus}}</ref> Nevertheless, their natural ability to multitask supported thriving crafts industries on Pollillus. Some Troigs eschewed most clothing and went about nude.<ref name="TRO 1" /> Others wore clothing, such as trousers and vests,<ref name="POTJ" /> albeit vests tailored to their four-armed physique.<ref name="SWCTP" /> Hairstyles were equally varied, with some Troigs wearing their locks in topknots and growing out mustaches and beards with beads strung over them. Troigs lived together in [[City/Legends|population centers]]; one such was [[Twin Cities (Pollillus)|Twin Cities]].<ref name="HNN 50" /> Those Troigs who emigrated from Pollillus were able to adapt to galactic-standard technology.<ref name="POTJ" />

Troigs were talented linguists. If one head learned a language, all heads could instinctively understand what the partner said.<ref name="TRO 1" /> Among the languages that some Troigs mastered were Basic and [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]].<ref name="POTJ" /> The species' own tongue was known as [[Troig (language)|Troig]].<ref name="OWSW" /> Indigenous names for Troigs followed a pattern whereby each head had its own name, which were joined together with the infix ''sin''. For example, a Troig with heads named Fode and Beed was known by the combined name FodesinBeed.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The system emphasized both the separateness of the personalities of a Troig's heads and the indivisibility of the full Troig.<ref name="TRO 1" /> In some transliterations, the ''sin'' was capitalized.<ref name="SOT 38" /> Similarly, the name that came later was only sometimes capitalized.<ref name="SWCTP" /> Among speakers of other languages, the two parts of the Troig name were often split so that the individual was known as, for example, Fode and Beed.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Some Troigs took a surname; one example was Annodue.<ref name="TRO 1" />

==History==
{{Quote|We can't just separate and kill Tabb, but leaving them together puts both of them at risk.|Doctor [[Senya Velop]] of [[Rhinnal State Medical Academy|Rhire Medical Academy]], on Dwuir's request to separate from his other head, Tabb|<ref name="HNN 50" />}}
[[File:Dwuirsintabb.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Dwuirsintabb requested head-separation surgery, but Troig technology was unable to accommodate the request.]]
Although the specific pressures that led to the development of a multi-headed species on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] remained a mystery to the galaxy as a whole, Pollillus served as the site of Troig evolution. Theories as to how their unique physiology might have arisen included the excellent defensive capabilities inherent in being able to look in more than one direction at once, although the lack of serious [[Hunting/Legends|predators]] on Pollilus cast some doubts on the full explanatory power of the theory.<ref name="TRO 1" />

By [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the Troigs had developed relatively simple technologies. Not long before the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] that [[Standard year/Legends|year]] by forces of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], visitors from the outside galaxy visited the world for the first time; these offworlders were [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassadors]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Intrigued by the prospect of a galaxy beyond their home [[Star system/Legends|star system]], Troigs began to leave the world.<ref name="TRO 1" />

Pollilus eventually became integrated into the [[Galactic community|wider galaxy]]. It became part of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> although its location just beyond the [[Koornacht Cluster/Legends|Koornacht Cluster]]<ref name="CSWE III 35" /> placed it within the more recently discovered systems known as [[the Negs]].<ref name="TEA" /> The world was incorporated as part of the [[Vannell sector/Legends|Vannell sector]].<ref name="CSWE III 35" /> As the planet became more integrated with the galaxy, more Troigs emigrated to find their fortunes abroad.<ref name="TRO 1" />

Troig named [[Dwuirsintabb]] on Pollillus made a public plea to be allowed to have his heads, Dwuir and Tabb, separated; Dwuir claimed that Tabb was "mentally disturbed and suicidal." A poll conducted by [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]], a galactic [[Media/Legends|media]] outlet, found that sixty-one percent of respondents supported Dwuir's wish to undergo head-separation surgery.<ref name="HNN 50" /> The matter remained unresolved after the Galactic Republic was [[Declaration of a New Order|replaced]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]<ref name="NEGAS" /> in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> By this point, the Troig government asked for outside help, as Troig technology remained incapable of providing a safe separation. No record of the outcome of Dwuirsintabb's saga survived, and his name fell out of galactic records by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the retirement of [[Senior Anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]]<ref name="NEGAS" /> in the days of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="EGAS viii">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>

The Troig homeworld remained neutral during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] (21&ndash;19 BBY), as it lay beyond the spheres of influence of both the Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. By [[137 ABY]], the planet fell within territory claimed by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Krayt]] as part of his [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Troigs in the galaxy==
{{Quote|A 15% gratuity will be added for parties greater than seven (or three and a half Troigs).|Menu for Dex's Diner|<ref name="DD">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/dexdiner/index.html|text=Dining at Dex's|int=Dining at Dex's}}</ref>}}
[[File:Story_4.jpg|thumb|left|200px|AndroosinLiann interviews [[Laslo Dorits]].]]
After the species made first contact with representatives of the Galactic Republic, many Troigs became enthralled by the prospect of visiting the [[Star/Legends|stars]] and therefore left their planet. The species' inherent extroversion made them natural [[entertainer]]s and event hosts. For example, the most famous Troig for many years was [[Fodesinbeed Annodue/Legends|Fodesinbeed Annodue]], one of the earliest members of his species to depart Pollillus. More popularly known as Fode and Beed, the Troig found employment as an announcer for the fast-paced sport of [[Podracing/Legends|Podracing]]. Within a year of his world's discovery by outsiders, Fode and Beed had become the most famous sportscaster in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] and the most famous Troig in the galaxy.<ref name="TRO 1" /> Annodue followed the [[Galactic Podracing Circuit/Legends|Galactic Podracing Circuit]] throughout the Outer Rim and became the voices of the sport for most enthusiasts.<ref name="POTJ" /> His ubiquity at the races placed him in the commentators' box during the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> in 32 BBY,<ref name="NEC" /> the year that the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Youngling/Legends|child]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] won the event.<ref name="TPM" /> Afterward, the Troig had to evade an angry mob who accused him of rigging the race. Despite the incident, Annodue appealed to a wide audience with Fode and Beed's bilingual commentating: Fode spoke Basic during races, while Beed spoke Huttese<ref name="POTJ" />&mdash;although Beed was able to speak Basic as well when circumstances required it.<ref name="EIR">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']]</ref> The Troig hosted a Podracing program called the ''[[Fode and Beed Show/Legends|Fode and Beed Show]]'' and an event at the [[Poodoo Lounge]] in Tatooine's city of [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] on at least one occasion<ref name="PRT" /> and remained an active announcer for at least the next decade.<ref name="KSW">''[[Kinect Star Wars]]''</ref>

Another Troig who found a place in the entertainment industry was [[AndroosinLiann]], who worked as the host of ''[[Essence]]'', a talk show broadcast from the planet [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]].<ref name="HNN 15">{{InsiderCite|72|Republic HoloNet News Core Edition 15:01:03}}</ref> AndroosinLiann interviewed the Human Republic [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Laslo Dorits]], who accused the Human [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of warmongering.<ref name="HNN 45" /> [[Unidentified Troig circus performer|Another Troig entertainer]] worked as a fire-eater in a [[Circus/Legends|circus]] that visited the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] at some point during the regime of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="WOSW 162" />

Not all offworld Troigs worked in the entertainment industry, though; for instance, [[Unidentified Troig pilot|one member]] of the species served as a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]]-for-hire.<ref name="RG:P 16">{{GamerCite|9|Rogues Gallery (Star Wars Gamer)|Rogues Gallery: Pilots for Hire}}</ref> The species also dispatched diplomats; [[Unidentified Troig diplomat|one such Troig]] owned the [[G2 repair droid/Legends|G2 repair droid]] called [[G2-9T/Legends|G2-9T]] but sold it to the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency at a bargain rate at some point after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]<ref name="EGTD 27">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. By the outbreak of the Clone Wars in 22 BBY,<ref name="NEC" /> Troigs had become well enough known on Coruscant that the [[Besalisk/Legends|Besalisk]] restauranteur [[Dexter Jettster/Legends|Dexter Jettster]] warned in the menu of his [[Dex's Diner/Legends|diner]] that he charged a fifteen percent gratuity to any party of more than three and a half Troigs.<ref name="DD" />

{{RPG}}
During the regime of the Galactic Empire, the Troig [[Pillaat and Nerro]] held a longstanding position as a [[Bartender/Legends|bartender]] at [[the Spyder]] [[Casino/Legends|casino]] on the planet Coruscant. He was skilled at using all four arms to serve customers and at keeping his patrons company. The Troig was quick to talk about clandestine activities in Imperial Center, especially after a bribe. For example, he gave a group of patrons information on the [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Kaa'to Leeachos]] on one occasion.<ref name="SOABS">''[[Under a Black Sun]]''</ref>{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Troig_concept_art.jpg|thumb|right|upright|An early production sketch of Fode and Beed shows the character with much shorter necks.]]
{{Quote|We went in, and we riffed&mdash;that's how it worked.|Greg Proops, on filming Fode and Beed's scenes for ''The Phantom Menace''|<ref name="VOEI" />}}
The Troig species was created during production of the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] when director [[George Lucas]] wanted a two-headed character to serve as the announcer during the film's Podracing sequence. Preliminary sketches of the character Fodesinbeed Annodue were created by artists [[Terryl Whitlatch]] and [[Iain McCaig]]. Various ideas presented by the artists included giving the species a wide torso with a more humanoid body; giving the species dark-gray skin, sharp claws, and evil-looking smirks; and putting the announcer in long robes. Although all of McCaig's and Whitlatch's concepts showed a species with two heads on a single body<ref name="AOSWEI 140-141">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]''</ref>&mdash;one atop the other in one of Whitlatch's drawings<ref name="EIIG" />&mdash;not all of them featured four arms.<ref name="AOSWEI 140-141" /> Most of the concepts featured two-legged beings, although one of Whitlatch's showed a tripedal creature.<ref name="EIIG" /> Lucas approved one of Whitlatch's designs for the final character's look.<ref name="AOSWEI 140-141" />

Comedians [[Scott Capurro]] and [[Greg Proops]] were hired to play the role of the announcer, with Capurro as Beed and Proops as Fode. Originally, [[Industrial Light & Magic]] (ILM) attempted to realize the Troig character by putting Capurro and Proops in elaborate makeup, a process that took several hours to complete. The actors then dressed in blue bodysuits and performed in front of a blue screen.<ref name="DB" /> The shoot occurred after principal photography had finished and was completed in a day,<ref name="VOEI">{{InsiderCite|48|Voices of Episode I}}</ref> but when the animators attempted to digitally place the actors' heads atop the character's body, the result was deemed too unrealistic and difficult to execute. Instead, ILM created the Troig announcer as a wholly computer-generated (CG) character. Although the character was originally slated to be named Fodesinbeed Annodue, the surname was dropped before the film was released.<ref name="DB" /> It was restored to the character with the publication of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 121]]'', a source that also [[canon]]ized as [[in-universe]] one of Whitlatch's concept drawings.<ref name="TRO 1" />

The shift from human heads on a CG body to a fully CG character is reflected in peripheral material from ''The Phantom Menace''. For example, the [[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace (comic series)|''Phantom Menace'' comic book]] depicts the character with heads that resemble the made-up Capurro and Proops.<ref name="TPM2" /> Similarly, in [[Hasbro]]'s first action figure of Annodue, released as "[[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] with 2-Headed Announcer" as part of the [[Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|''Star Wars: Episode I'' toy line]] in 1999, the character resembles the older version with heads based on those of Capurro and Proops in makeup.<ref name="EITL">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|pack=Jabba the Hutt with 2-Headed Announcer|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/episodeIjabbaannouncer.asp}}</ref> However, Hasbro corrected the character to match his final on-screen appearance with the release of the "Fode and Beed" pack, part of the ''[[Star Wars: Power of the Jedi]]'' line, in [[2000]].<ref name="POTJ" />

[[File:Capurrosinproops_bts.jpg|thumb|left|Troig announcer Fodesinbeed Annodue was originally intended to be created from the heads of Scott Capurro and Greg Proops paired with a computer-generated body.]]
Annodue has made the most appearances in ''[[Star Wars]]'' material of the Troig species, notably in adaptations of ''The Phantom Menace'' such as the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]], [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)|junior novelization]], comic book, [[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace Cine-Manga|PhotoComic]], and [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|video game]], but also in spin-off materials such as ''[[Star Wars: Anakin's Speedway]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|Star Wars Episode I: Racer]]'', and ''[[Star Wars: Yoda's Challenge Activity Center]]''. Other material introduced new Troig characters, such as DwuirsinTabb and AndroosinLiann in [[HoloNet News (original website)|''HoloNet News'']],<ref name="HNN 50" /><ref name="HNN 45">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|news/13228_4.html|Stark Veterans Blast Amidala}}</ref> and a nameless Troig [[Pazaak/Legends|pazaak]] dealer in the introduction to [[Star Wars Tales 23|''Star Wars Tales'' 23]], who runs a match played by [[Dark Horse Comics]] editor [[Jeremy Barlow]].<ref name="T23">[[Star Wars Tales 23|''Star Wars Tales'' 23]]</ref> Author [[Abel G. Peña]] considered [[Retroactive continuity|retroactively]] identifying a [[Unidentified Dyclops pirate|two-headed character]] from the [[1986]] [[Marvel Comics|Marvel]] comic book [[Droids (1986) 3|''Droids'' (1986) 3]] as a Troig for an [[The Droids Re-Animated|article]] he co-wrote with [[Rich Handley]] for the [[Star Wars Blog]]. However, the anatomy was not close enough, so the authors instead gave a new name to the two-headed species, [[Dyclops]].<ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=posts/50801413|board=Literature|thread=What's This? More Droids from Handley and Peña?|user=Halagad_Ventor|date=2013-06-15|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316143709/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/whats-this-more-droids-from-handley-and-pe%C3%B1a.50012958}}</ref>

''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', a book published by [[Del Rey]] in [[2006]] and written by [[Ann Margaret Lewis (real person)|Ann Margaret Lewis]] and [[Helen Keier]], includes an entry on Troigs that contradicts most other sources in two key areas. First, the book claims that the species' homeworld, Pollillus, is located in the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] region of the galaxy.<ref name="NEGAS" /> This contradicts other sources, which place it in the Core Worlds.<ref name="TEA" /> Secondly, Lewis and Keier describe Troigs as "humanoid," a description in direct contrast to the species' multiple heads and arms, as well as tails.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Game statistics allow players of the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' from [[Wizards of the Coast]] to portray Troig characters. The rules afford them some protection from surprise and a lessened penalty for doing two tasks simultaneously.<ref name="SOT 38" /> Amended statistics published online provide Troigs with even more ability to perform multiple tasks at once.<ref name="JC" />

In the adventure [[Under a Black Sun|''Star Wars: Edge of the Empire: Shadows of a Black Sun'']], for the ''[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire]]'' roleplaying game from [[Fantasy Flight Games]], the encounter between the Troig Pillaat and Nerro and the player characters is optional; the characters may instead opt to visit another location to gather information about Kaa'to Leeachos. However, the adventure allows for the possibility of visiting all three, so this article assumes such a full completion of the scenario.<ref name="SOABS" />
